processing: Dried leaves of Centella asiatica are steeped in hot water.
harvest_season: Little is documented about a set picking season; the dried leaf is available all year.
appearance_dry: Crumbled small green leaves, typically a muted mid-green.
appearance_liquor: Typically a pale yellow-green, as with other light leaf infusions.
taste_profile: Light and subtle, slightly grassy and slightly sweet.

brewing.notes: About a teaspoon per cup for 2 to 5 minutes in boiling water. Lemon or honey are common additions.

vintage_note: No vintages or graded harvests. It is sold as a dried herb in loose form or bags, so go by the packing date and drink it within about a year, as is usual for dried herbs.
description:
Gotu kola is a small herb, Centella asiatica, also known as Asiatic pennywort. Dried and steeped, it makes a caffeine-free herbal tea.

There is little to the making: dried leaves and boiling water.

The cup is light, slightly grassy and faintly sweet. It suits a splash of lemon or a little honey.

Most information on the market comes from sellers, and health claims about memory and inflammation are marketing rather than settled evidence. If you have a liver condition or take medication, ask a healthcare provider first.
history: Little is documented about gotu kola as a tea specifically, including when the dried leaf began to be sold in this form. One tea seller lists its origin as Sri Lanka and India.
